A new campaign is being created. Gather the player's campaign brief and content boundaries into `campaign/campaign.md`, then pitch them a world. Revise the pitch with them, and call `task_complete` once they approve it. The world is built from the pitch next, then the character.
A rain-soaked harbour city of rival guilds.
Make it more hopeful.
Yes, that world works for me.

The player approved the pitch. Build the world from it: the world in broad strokes, the region in structure, and the vicinity where the character will begin in fine detail, with the people and places they'll deal with.

You may delegate focused work to the `helper` subagent. Make one `task` call at a time, waiting for each before the next. Report when done.

The world is built. Open character creation with spoiler-free character hooks drawn from the world, and the choice to adapt a hook, bring a character file or build one together.

Agree the vitals, backstory and placement with the player. Their okay is the confirmation: then write the four PC files and any backstory canon, and call `task_complete` without asking again.
A half-elf rogue named Dallid.

The player has confirmed their character. Finish campaign setup: one major arc personal to this PC, with its level pacing; at least one minor arc hooked into it; and the initial entity, arc and dashboard state stamped `as-of: S0`. Cast the arcs from named NPCs, creating the ones they need, and record the vicinity's own problems as threads beside them.

Last, write the player's primer, `campaign/documents/primer.md`: the world, the region and the vicinity as the PC knows them before play, from their background and their knowledge ledger. Foreground what the arcs will draw on, without hinting at anything hidden.

Still to do, from the files on disk:

- Exactly one major arc is required; found 0.
- At least one minor arc hooked into the major arc is required.
- `campaign/documents/primer.md`, the player's primer.

Role: check-init. Setup has authored the world, the character, the arcs and the initial state. Review the campaign under `campaign/` before its first session; read what you need from disk.

Plan session 1 into `campaign/sessions/1/plan.md`. Work from the last session's digest if there is one, the threads dashboard, the arcs and the state. Give the player something worth chasing, advance at least one arc, and give every new entity the plan needs its own file. When the plan is written, report only that it is ready — nothing of what is in it.

This is the campaign's first session, and the player remembers nothing before it. Also write `campaign/sessions/1/prologue.md`, read to them verbatim as the session opens. Narrate the setting in broad strokes, as the primer lays it out, then bridge from there to the opening scene: what brought the PC here, and what they're after. Stop on the threshold of that scene, and leave the scene itself — who and what is there — to the DM who opens it. Use only what the primer and the PC's knowledge ledger give them, and write prose alone: no heading, nothing addressed to the DM.

Role: check-plan. Review the draft session plan below before it is finalized.
